caption:
Anything in localStorage can be read by any JavaScript running on your page. That includes a third-party script, a compromised npm package, or code injected through an XSS bug (a hole that lets an attacker run their script on your site).

One injected line can send your users' tokens to someone else's server.

An httpOnly cookie is the common alternative: the browser sends it with requests, but JavaScript can't read it at all. Pair it with the Secure and SameSite flags.

It doesn't fix XSS. It stops XSS from walking away with the token.

Source: OWASP HTML5 Security Cheat Sheet (Local Storage).
